answer: An agent market requires a $100 bond, locked for 30 days, for each identity eligible to bid on jobs, whether surveying a grove, mapping a dune, or tracking the sun's zenith. Each bonded identity gets one bid slot per round; extra accounts without bonds get none. An attacker seeking 1,000 slots must immobilize $100,000 for a month, paying financing or opportunity costs. This makes influence capital-bound rather than account-count-bound.
